claims.statement: Every web UI submit carries run_name "chess-web" and tag "web" (WEB_TRACE) plus metadata surface "web", uses multitaskStrategy reject, and puts the game's recorded settings in config.configurable via configurableOf (version first, then every setting key), which lets web traffic be separated from Studio/SDK runs in LangSmith.
The web client's retry sends an empty input to resume a pending turn, because a fresh go would be rejected while a turn is pending.

chat_model names the chat model after the model part of its spec so gateway LLM spans appear under the model name rather than ChatOpenAI, and caps output at MAX_TOKENS = 64000 including reasoning, lowered to the model's own output limit or half of a smaller context window, with a max_tokens from model_kwargs replacing the budget.
System 1 classifier requests are traced under the run names systemone.rank, systemone.heats and systemone.final.

GatewayRanker retries only transient errors, with max_attempts=3 total and backoff_seconds (0.5 s then 1 s) between attempts, and the server's classifiers use the shared pool's HTTP clients with a 15 s timeout, so a request whose attempts all time out blocks for roughly 46.5 s before RankingFailed.

RankingFailed carries the elapsed time and completed calls of the failed ranking, and a skipped System 1 decision stores both, so ply telemetry latency_ms and the turn's latency include time lost to failed rankings.
When ranking fails, a SystemOneMiddleware with has_model=True freezes a skipped decision and the LLM plays unaided, while has_model=False (policy systemone) re-raises RankingFailed and fails the run.

CallRecorder records a Call only when a provider response ends and drops errored provider calls in on_llm_error, so a turn's recorded calls undercount failed or stalled attempts that traces still show.

turn.latency_ms is the wall time inside ChessCore.wrap_model_call plus each extension's turn_latency_ms (System 1 ranking, counted once across retries), folded in when the turn finalizes or is abandoned; it excludes summarization and graph overhead, so it is lower than root-trace latency.

Each illegal or unparseable reply triggers feedback and another model call while illegal_attempts < max_retries (default 3); after that a resignation terminal_intent with reason illegal_moves is set. The counter lives on the durable turn record, so a resume after a provider error keeps the remaining budget and a turn gets at most four parsed replies.
Provider exceptions that look like context overflow are re-raised from wrap_model_call as ContextBudgetError, including when the overflow follows a completed call, leaving the turn pending.

ChessContext defaults are policy hybrid, model langsmith:baseten/zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash with no reasoning_effort and empty model_kwargs, memory off, threshold 0.9 with the margin gate, tournament_threshold unset, k 5, systemone_model semif-qwen3.5-4b, and with_eval and with_nouls off, so summarization only runs when a caller turns memory on.
The UCI adapter's fallback bestmove is System 1's fallback_move when it is in the root pool, otherwise a seeded random legal move, or 0000 when no move is available.

resolve_context migrates the assistant context and then config configurable to the current settings version (dropping unknown keys and reading a source without version as current), merges them with the later source winning, treats an explicit null as a reset to the default, and validates the merged values with ChessContext so a bad setting fails the run up front.

With memory on, summarization triggers at 70% of the model's input limit; gateway models get a profile with max_input_tokens equal to the known context window minus the output budget, and build_agent raises ChessContractError when the model has no known input limit.

policy systemone builds no chat model, so memory is ignored, and sets both System 1 thresholds to 0 with has_model=False so System 1 always plays, while policy llm with fixed_topology (as on the server) installs the no-op NoSystemOne placeholder that keeps the node but ranks nothing.
System 1 policies require TYPESAFE_API_KEY and TYPESAFE_BASE_URL, and a gateway or TypeSafe setting that is set but blank is rejected as an error rather than treated as unset.

When a model call records a completed response and then fails, wrap_model_call keeps the completed calls on the turn and writes a failed_call marker; after_model re-raises the original error in the same run, and because the error is held only in instance memory, a later resume clears the marker and calls the model again.

An empty-input resume of a pending turn finalizes an already validated proposal or terminal intent without calling the model again; otherwise it clears the decision fields and restores allowed_moves from the turn's initial_allowed. A new chat message while a turn is pending is rejected, and a new position request abandons the pending turn.

The System 1 HTTP client pair is one ClientPool per process, created lazily under a lock so concurrent first uses make one pair, kept in clients.py because langgraph loads graph.py under a generated module name; the FastAPI lifespan, merged with the Agent Server's, closes it on shutdown and the next get creates a fresh pair.

The web table shows a ChessCore rejection (state error) as a dismissible "Move rejected" banner, a failed run or submit as an inline error message, a 401/403 from the Agent Server as an API-key banner, silently drops a busy-run rejection, and for a pending turn locks the board and offers only a Retry button.
The web new-game dialog offers memory only when GET /ui/model-limit, backed by the cached model_limit, reports a known input limit for the model.

When the Agent Server calls the graph factory without an execution runtime (state reads, updates, introspection), make_graph returns a shape graph with every node switched off that needs no model, clients or credentials.

StallRetry retries only a stalled response stream (langchain_openai StreamChunkTimeoutError, or nothing when langchain_openai is absent) once, with no delay and on_failure error, inside the same turn; a second stall re-raises so the run fails with the turn pending for Retry.
StallRetry runs inside ChessCore.wrap_model_call, so the time spent on a stalled attempt counts toward turn.latency_ms while the stalled attempt itself records no Call.
CallRecorder marks a recorded call cost_complete False when its request carried hosted tools, because token prices do not cover those tools' own charges.

The server builds the chat model with surface server, which accepts only an allowlist of request arguments from model_kwargs and holds back account resources such as hosted tools, and the graph's run metadata records the values actually sent.
